exp.desc:
- Accounts to year end
- Introduced e-invoicing
- Contact for auditors

cl.p1: after 22 years, my employer, a builders’ merchant, is closing its local branch at the end of the year. I ran the accounts there from purchase ledger to year end, latterly as the only qualified member of staff with one assistant.
cl.p2: At 54 I bring what an accounts department needs: calm at month end, a feel for when a number is wrong, and good relationships with external accountants and auditors. Last year I introduced electronic invoicing myself. I know construction from the supplier side and would quickly learn the contractor side.

cl.p1: why would anyone change jobs at 58? In my case it is simple: my employer is moving production abroad, and I want to spend my remaining working years where parts are actually made.
cl.p2: I have thirty years in quality assurance in metalworking, fourteen of them leading a department of eight. I have taken two sites through certification and audited suppliers across Europe. What I can pass on is experience of mistakes you do not make twice.
cl.p3: I do not need a management role. I need my experience to be useful.
